description: Indulge in the authentic taste of Liguria with this Focaccia Genovese recipe, a classic Italian flatbread. Made with rich olive oil and fragrant rosemary, it boasts a delightfully crisp crust and a soft, airy interior. This beloved bread is perfect as an appetizer, a side to any meal, or simply enjoyed on its own.

ingredients.notes: plus more for drizzling and pan

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the lukewarm water and fresh yeast. If using active dry yeast, let it bloom for 5-10 minutes until foamy. Stir in 1 tablespoon of olive oil.

instructions.title: Mix the Dough
instructions.text: Add the flour and fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 10-15 minutes until it is smooth and elastic. Alternatively, use a stand mixer with a dough hook.

instructions.title: First Rise
instructions.text: Lightly oil a clean bowl with olive oil. Place the dough in the bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a damp tea towel and let it rise in a warm place for 1-1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.

instructions.title: Prepare and Dimple the Dough
instructions.text: Generously oil a 25x35 cm (10x14 inch) baking sheet with olive oil. Gently transfer the risen dough to the prepared baking sheet. Using your fingertips, gently stretch and press the dough to fill the pan, creating characteristic dimples across the surface. Be careful not to deflate it completely.

instructions.title: Second Rise and Top
instructions.text: Cover the baking sheet loosely with plastic wrap or a tea towel and let the focaccia rise again for another 30-45 minutes, or until it looks puffy. Preheat your oven to 220C (425F) during the last 15 minutes of the second rise. Drizzle generously with more extra virgin olive oil, then sprinkle with fresh rosemary leaves and coarse sea salt.

instructions.title: Bake the Focaccia
instructions.text: Bake the focaccia in the preheated oven for 20-30 minutes, or until it is golden brown on top and cooked through. The crust should be crisp and the bottom should sound hollow when tapped.

instructions.title: Cool and Serve
instructions.text: Once baked, immediately transfer the focaccia to a wire rack to cool slightly. Drizzle with a final touch of fresh olive oil if desired. Slice and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy the authentic taste of Liguria!

tips: For an extra crispy crust, place a pan of hot water on the bottom rack of your oven during baking to create steam.
Do not skimp on good quality extra virgin olive oil; it is crucial for the authentic flavor and texture of Focaccia Genovese.
Focaccia is best enjoyed fresh on the day it is baked. If you have leftovers, refresh them in a warm oven for a few minutes.
article:
The aroma of freshly baked bread, infused with fragrant rosemary and rich olive oil, is one of life's simplest pleasures. Few breads capture this essence quite like Focaccia Genovese. Hailing from the sun-drenched region of Liguria in Italy, this iconic flatbread is more than just a side dish; it's a testament to the beauty of minimal ingredients and masterful technique. If you've ever dreamt of recreating that authentic Italian bakery experience in your own kitchen, preparing a Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil loaf is an incredibly rewarding journey. It’s a staple of Italian baking, known for its distinct texture and irresistible flavor profile.

## What is Focaccia Genovese?
Focaccia Genovese, or "fugassa" in the local Ligurian dialect, is a specific type of focaccia that originates from Genoa, the capital of Liguria. Unlike some thicker, more bread-like focaccias found elsewhere in Italy, the Genovese version is traditionally thinner, characterized by its incredibly airy, open crumb, a wonderfully crisp bottom, and a signature dimpled surface that acts as a reservoir for olive oil and coarse sea salt.

The defining features of an authentic Focaccia Genovese include a generous amount of high-quality extra virgin olive oil, both in the dough and drizzled over the top before baking, and a liberal sprinkling of flaky sea salt. Often, fresh rosemary is incorporated, providing an aromatic counterpoint to the richness of the olive oil. It’s not just a bread; it’s a cultural icon, frequently enjoyed for breakfast with coffee, as a mid-morning snack, or alongside various meals throughout the day. Its simplicity belies a depth of flavor and texture that makes it universally beloved, embodying the very soul of Italian baking.

## Ingredients You Need for Focaccia Genovese
Creating a truly exceptional Focaccia Genovese begins with selecting the right ingredients. Quality over quantity is key here, as each component plays a vital role in the final texture and taste.

*   **High-Quality Bread Flour:** While all-purpose flour can work, bread flour with its higher protein content will give you a better chew and structure.
*   **Active Dry or Instant Yeast:** Essential for that beautiful rise and airy crumb.
*   **Warm Water:** Around 100-110°F (38-43°C) is perfect for activating the yeast.
*   **Extra Virgin Olive Oil (EVOO):** This is non-negotiable. Use the best quality you can afford. It imparts flavor, tenderizes the crumb, and creates the crispy crust. You'll need it for the dough, oiling the pan, and drizzling on top.
*   **Fine Sea Salt:** For seasoning the dough.
*   **Flaky Sea Salt:** For sprinkling on top before baking, providing bursts of briny flavor and a satisfying crunch.
*   **Fresh Rosemary:** Stripped from the stem and roughly chopped, this adds the quintessential aromatic note.
*   **A Pinch of Sugar:** To help activate the yeast and give it a little food to get started.

## Step-by-Step Instructions to Make Focaccia Genovese
Making Focaccia Genovese is a labor of love, but the process is straightforward and incredibly rewarding.

**Step 1: Activate the Yeast**
In a large bowl, combine the warm water, yeast, and sugar. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy. This indicates your yeast is active and ready to work.

**Step 2: Mix the Dough**
Add the flour and fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Pour in about 2 tablespoons of your good quality extra virgin olive oil. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms. It will be quite sticky, which is exactly what you want for a high-hydration focaccia.

**Step 3: Knead (or Stretch and Fold)**
Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Knead for about 5-7 minutes until it becomes somewhat smoother and more elastic. Alternatively, for a less hands-on approach, you can use the stretch and fold method: every 20-30 minutes during the first rise, wet your hands, gently stretch a portion of the dough up, and fold it over itself. Rotate the bowl and repeat 3-4 times. This builds gluten without intensive kneading.

**Step 4: First Rise**
Lightly oil a large bowl with olive oil. Place the dough in the bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover the bowl tightly with plastic wrap or a damp tea towel. Let it rise in a warm place for 1 to 2 hours, or until it has doubled in size.

**Step 5: Prepare the Baking Pan**
Generously coat a 9x13-inch baking pan (or a similar size) with extra virgin olive oil. Don't be shy – this oil creates the signature crispy bottom.

**Step 6: Stretch the Dough**
Gently transfer the risen dough to the prepared baking pan. Using your oiled fingertips, gently press and stretch the dough to fill the pan. If the dough resists and springs back, cover it with plastic wrap and let it rest for 10-15 minutes before continuing to stretch. This allows the gluten to relax.

**Step 7: Second Rise and Dimpling**
Once the dough is stretched, cover the pan lightly with plastic wrap or a tea towel. Let it rise again for another 30-45 minutes. After the second rise, generously drizzle more extra virgin olive oil over the top of the dough. Using your oiled fingertips, create deep dimples all over the surface of the focaccia, pressing down until you almost touch the bottom of the pan. These dimples will hold the olive oil and create those delightful pockets of flavor.

**Step 8: Flavoring and Baking**
Sprinkle the top generously with flaky sea salt and fresh rosemary. Preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C). Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the Focaccia Genovese is deeply golden brown on top and beautifully crisp on the bottom.

**Step 9: Cool**
Once baked, immediately transfer the focaccia to a wire rack to cool slightly. This prevents the bottom from becoming soggy. Slice and enjoy warm!

## Pro Tips for the Best Focaccia Genovese
Achieving that perfect, authentic Focaccia Genovese isn't just about following steps; a few expert tips can elevate your baking to another level.

*   **Embrace the Stickiness:** A high-hydration dough is key to an airy, open crumb. Don't be tempted to add too much extra flour if your dough feels sticky. Oiling your hands when handling the dough can help manage it.
*   **Quality EVOO is Paramount:** This cannot be stressed enough. The flavor of your extra virgin olive oil will shine through, so invest in a good one. It's not just a cooking fat; it's a primary flavor component.
*   **Don't Skimp on the Oil:** Generously oiling the pan ensures that coveted crispy bottom. Drizzling extra oil over the top before dimpling and baking keeps the focaccia moist and adds richness.
*   **Deep Dimples:** When dimpling, don't be afraid to press down firmly with oiled fingers. These indentations are crucial for trapping the olive oil and creating the characteristic irregular texture.
*   **Hot Oven, Quick Bake:** Baking at a relatively high temperature helps create a beautiful crust and ensures the interior cooks through without drying out.
*   **Listen to Your Dough:** Pay attention to its feel and how it rises. Ambient temperature and humidity can affect rising times, so adjust accordingly. Patience is a virtue in bread making.

## Serving Suggestions for Focaccia Genovese
The beauty of Focaccia Genovese lies in its versatility. It's delicious on its own, but it also makes a wonderful accompaniment to a variety of dishes.

*   **Simple Snack:** Enjoy a piece warmed, perhaps with a little extra drizzle of your best olive oil for dipping. This is how it's often eaten as a mid-morning snack in Liguria.
*   **With Meals:** It's an excellent bread to serve alongside hearty soups, fresh salads, or pasta dishes. Its porous texture is perfect for soaking up delicious sauces.
*   **Appetizer Platter:** Arrange slices on a board with cured meats, cheeses, olives, and perhaps a balsamic glaze or olive tapenade.
*   **Sandwich Base:** Slice horizontally and fill with your favorite deli meats, cheeses, roasted vegetables, or pesto for a fantastic sandwich.
*   **Breakfast Treat:** In Genoa, it's common to dip Focaccia Genovese into your morning coffee or cappuccino. Don't knock it till you've tried it!
*   **Bruschetta Alternative:** Top toasted pieces with fresh tomatoes and basil for a twist on classic bruschetta.

## Variations and Substitutions for Focaccia Genovese
While the traditional Focaccia Genovese is perfect as is, you can certainly experiment with variations to suit your taste or dietary needs.

*   **Toppings:** Beyond rosemary, consider adding thin slices of red onion, cherry tomatoes (halved and pressed into the dimples), pitted olives, thinly sliced garlic, or a sprinkle of dried oregano or thyme. Add these after dimpling and before the final olive oil drizzle and salt.
*   **Cheese:** A sprinkle of Parmesan or Pecorino Romano can be added during the last 5-10 minutes of baking for a cheesy crust.
*   **Spicy Kick:** A pinch of red pepper flakes can add a subtle warmth.
*   **Flour Blends:** While bread flour is ideal, you can experiment with replacing a small portion (up to 25%) with whole wheat flour for a nuttier flavor, or semolina flour for added chewiness.
*   **Gluten-Free:** While not traditional, many gluten-free flour blends can be used to make focaccia. Be aware that the texture will be different, often denser, but still delicious. Follow the specific instructions for your chosen GF flour blend.
*   **Vegan:** Focaccia Genovese is naturally vegan, making it a fantastic option for those avoiding animal products.

Baking your own Focaccia Genovese is more than just following a recipe; it's an immersive experience in Italian baking tradition. From the simple, pure ingredients to the satisfying process of kneading and dimpling, each step brings you closer to a truly remarkable bread. The reward is a golden, aromatic masterpiece, perfect for sharing, or for savoring a quiet moment of culinary bliss. So, gather your ingredients, embrace the process, and prepare to be transported to the sun-drenched coasts of Liguria with every delicious bite.
